atomic_journal_model.protocol: Checksummed append-only ADMIT/SLOT/CLOSE frames. ADMIT must be durable before slot launch; first durable deterministic SLOT event wins; CLOSE is the sole block commit marker; both numerical replay channels rebuild from one deduplicated closed row; missing/torn slots fail closed as score 1; late/conflicting overwrites are ignored/quarantined. Recovery truncates/quarantines an invalid torn tail to the last valid frame boundary before retrying.

systems_precedent.sqlite_atomic_commit: SQLite documents crash-consistent atomic commit and explicitly uses simulated incomplete/out-of-order writes in crash tests. This supports crash injection as a validation method but is not evidence that the role-local Python framing survives arbitrary filesystem behavior.
systems_precedent.sqlite_wal: SQLite WAL uses append frames and a commit marker before checkpointing back to database state; this is a systems precedent for making an append log authoritative and caches/reconstructed state secondary.

measurement_validity_rules: Durable admission is a scientific precondition, not merely an implementation detail: no outcome may be launched or accepted before the complete admitted slot set, deadline and exposure denominator are durable.

A slot result is scientific evidence only after its complete durable record. A torn result must remain missing/fail-closed unless the same logical attempt is retried with the same deterministic event identity.
The first durable payload for a deterministic slot identity wins. Conflicting retries and results after the frozen deadline/close cannot overwrite evidence.

CLOSE is the only durable block commit marker. The process and planned-exposure channels must replay from the same unique closed row rather than persist separate channel appends that could diverge across a crash.
Numerical e-process/root caches are reconstructible implementation state, not scientific truth.

A torn tail must be truncated/quarantined to the last checksummed valid prefix before any retry append; simply appending after unreadable garbage makes later valid frames unreachable to prefix replay.
scope_guards: The validation models a single-writer ordered append stream with durable-prefix semantics; it does not establish correctness under arbitrary corruption of earlier durable bytes, broken fsync, storage reordering, or unsynchronized multi-writer appends.
The 781 cut points and 1000 random campaigns are software/model stress, not production failure probabilities.
The protocol does not establish optimal fsync frequency, performance overhead or a preferred production storage engine.
No statistical tolerance, alpha allocation, block-size policy or dual-channel estimand was changed by this durability work.
No forbidden semantic inputs were read and no connector-discovery mutation occurred.
